---
title: "PCA for Demographic Controls"
author: "Manolis Giannitselis"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
```

```{r example-data, echo=FALSE}
# Small simulated stand-in for the real county-year panel, so this file
# runs standalone. See README for the real construction of control_df.
set.seed(42)
control_df <- tibble(
  county_name     = rep(paste0("County_", 1:20), each = 5),
  year            = rep(2015:2019, times = 20),
  pct_employed    = rnorm(100, 0.60, 0.05),
  avg_educ        = rnorm(100, 13, 1.5),
  total_pop       = rnorm(100, 50000, 15000),
  pct_female      = rnorm(100, 0.50, 0.02),
  avg_age         = rnorm(100, 38, 4),
  pct_white       = rnorm(100, 0.70, 0.15),
  avg_income_real = rnorm(100, 45000, 8000)
)
```

```{r run-pca}
n_pcs <- 4

# center/scale = TRUE standardizes each variable first, so population
# (tens of thousands) doesn't swamp percentage variables (0-1).
pca <- prcomp(
  control_df %>% select(-county_name, -year),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = TRUE
)

summary(pca)
```

```{r scree-plot}
# Used to pick n_pcs: keep components up to the "elbow".
screeplot(pca, type = "lines")
```

```{r loadings}
# Loadings = which raw variables each component is built from.
print(pca$rotation[, 1:n_pcs], digits = 2)
```

```{r extract-scores}
# Scores = each county-year's value on each component; this is what
# gets merged back into the panel and used as a regression control.
scores <- as_tibble(pca$x[, 1:n_pcs], rownames = "row_id") %>%
  setNames(c("row_id", paste0("PC", 1:n_pcs))) %>%
  mutate(row_id = as.integer(row_id)) %>%
  select(-row_id) %>%
  bind_cols(control_df %>% select(county_name, year), .)

head(scores)
```

```{r real-data, eval=FALSE}
# In the actual project, control_df is built like this from the full
# panel (agg_panel_trim), and scores are joined back on before running
# the DiD/IV regressions in did-analysis/:

control_df <- agg_panel_trim %>%
  select(
    county_name, year,
    pct_employed, avg_educ, total_pop,
    pct_female, avg_age, pct_white, avg_income_real
  ) %>%
  na.omit()

panel_with_controls <- panel %>%
  left_join(scores, by = c("county_name", "year"))
```
